title: Bounded below compactness of an integral constructible complex
statement:
Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $A_T$ and $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K$ belong to [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For every small family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ of objects of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ with one common cohomological lower bound, the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_T}(K,M_i)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_T}\bigl(K,\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism in the derived category of $A$-modules. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}$ is global derived Hom (derived global sections of derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]), and coproducts are derived coproducts of module sheaves; the lower bound may be any integer, with shifts understood as in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12, with a shift for an arbitrary common lower bound; the integral category is identified by Proposition 6.8.11(3).

proof.text: First establish the bounded-below cohomology calculation for an arbitrary commutative ring sheaf R on the pro-etale site of a qcqs scheme S. The module category is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with the diagram category chosen to be the one-object identity category. Given M_i with a common lower bound N, choose representatives E_i with E_i^q=0 for q<N using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Their termwise sum represents the derived coproduct by [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. Choose the affine weakly contractible hypercover U_bullet of S supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-computes-bounded-complex], RΓ(S,M_i) is the total complex of E_i^q(U_p), and the same formula computes the coproduct. Evaluation on U_p preserves sums by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits]. In total degree r only N≤q≤r and p=r-q occur, so interchanging the sum over i with this finite sum identifies the total complexes, including their differentials and coprojections. Therefore the canonical map ⊕_i RΓ(S,M_i)→RΓ(S,⊕_i M_i) is an isomorphism. This proves the integral ring-sheaf version directly, rather than applying the existing rational-coefficient pushforward lemma.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 via Lemma 6.3.14(1); explicit ringed proof of Stacks Tag 09A3 from Tags 09A1/09A2/0946/0935

proof.text: We use a local form of the desired property. For a qcqs S, a commutative ring sheaf R, and B bounded above, let C_S(B) mean: for every qcqs pro-etale object W→S, global RHom on W out of B|_W commutes with every small family with a common lower bound. All coefficient sheaves in this argument are inverse images of R; when tensoring with A-complexes, fix the A-algebra structure on R and write R_Z=i^{-1}R for a closed immersion i. Write H(B,M)=Rℋom_R(B,M). If B∈D^{≤b} and M∈D^{≥N}, then H(B,M)∈D^{≥N-b}. Here are details that do not assume an injective resolution starts in exactly degree N. Choose bounded-below K-injective representatives using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. The global-sections theorem [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], applied on the slice site and to M|_W[r], together with shift compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], gives H^r RHom_W(B|_W,M|_W)=Hom_D(B|_W,M|_W[r]). For r<N-b this group is zero by orthogonality of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], since M[r] lies in D^{≥N-r} with N-r>b. Restriction is exact. Also [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] preserves K-injective resolutions and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies the restricted H with H on the slice. For affine weakly contractible W, step 1's exact-evaluation statement identifies these zero groups with the sections of the cohomology sheaf H^r(H(B,M)) on W. Such W cover every affine object, by the degree-zero part of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover]. Therefore that sheaf is zero. This proves the asserted uniform bound on internal Hom. These identifications apply to arbitrary B, not just locally free complexes. For each site object W→S, clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] gives a canonical equivalence of sites W_proet≃S_proet/W, preserving covering families; strict equality of independently chosen small skeleta is not needed. Transport the restricted ring sheaf R|_W and its modules along this equivalence. Their actions and restrictions are sectionwise as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so the slice K-injective and internal-Hom theorems above apply with these coefficients. This uses only the site-equivalence clause, not the constant-ring identification in clauses (2) and (3); the completed coefficient ring need not be constant.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(3),(4), details of the boundedness and restriction argument

proof.text: Here is the locality argument for C_S, including the distinction between internal and global Hom. For any uniformly bounded-below family M_i, form α:⊕_i H(B,M_i)→H(B,⊕_i M_i). Its source and target have the common lower bound N-b from step 2. By step 1, RΓ(W,α) is exactly the global Hom comparison for the restricted family on every qcqs W. Conversely, if these comparisons are isomorphisms on every qcqs W, the cone of α is zero: test on affine weakly contractible W, where exact evaluation identifies derived evaluation with evaluation on complexes; its cohomology sections all vanish. Such W cover every object, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover] applied to affine objects, so every cohomology sheaf of the cone is zero. Slice restriction of α is its corresponding comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; restriction also commutes with sums (the sheafified sectionwise description in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]). Thus C_S(B) can be checked on a pro-etale covering by qcqs objects V_a: for any qcqs W, the objects W×_S V_a cover W, all their further qcqs slices are allowed in C_{V_a}, and the preceding cone test shows α|_{V_a}=0 on cones, hence α is an isomorphism on W. The qcqs fibre products and covering operations are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. The bound b is fixed before this test, so no unbounded totalization is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(3),(4), proof of pro-etale locality for bounded-above sources

proof.text: The class C_S is closed under shifts, finite sums, direct summands and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles of bounded-above objects. Indeed H sends source triangles to triangles and respects shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; the comparisons α form a morphism of triangles. Direct sums of these triangles are triangles, as seen on their mapping-cone complexes using [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. In the long exact cohomology sequences, if the comparisons for two vertices are isomorphisms, exactness gives it for the third; a comparison on a direct summand is the corresponding direct summand of the comparison. The unit R belongs to C_S because RHom_R(R,M)=RΓ(S,M), and the same identity holds on every slice, so step 1 applies. Consequently R⊗_A^L P belongs to C_S for every bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules: each projective term is a summand of a finite free module, and the finite sequence of stupid-truncation triangles builds P from these terms. All operations are finite; no compact-generation assertion is being used.

If j:U→S is a quasi-compact open immersion, then j_! carries C_U to C_S. The exact adjunction j_!⊣j^{-1} is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. It induces a derived adjunction: restriction sends K-injectives to K-injectives, since maps into a restricted K-injective from an acyclic complex are adjoint to maps from its acyclic exact j_!-image. Apply the chain adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to obtain Hom_D(j_!B,M[r])=Hom_D(B,j^{-1}M[r]) for every r. By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and shift compatibility from step 2, these are the cohomology groups of the global derived Homs. The bijections are natural in M and hence intertwine the canonical coproduct comparisons. Since coproducts of A-modules are exact, the property C_U(B) implies that the comparison on S is an isomorphism on every cohomology group, and thus an isomorphism in D(A). Restriction is exact and preserves coproducts by its sectionwise restriction and sheafification description, so the common lower bound on M_i remains the same on U. The argument applies on every qcqs slice W, with U_W=U×_S W; this is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], and restriction of j_! is the extension by zero for U_W, directly from its presheaf definition in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. This proves the required comparison on every W.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(2), specialized to the quasi-compact open immersions needed here

proof.text: Let i:Z→S be closed with quasi-compact open complement h:V→S, and suppose L on Z is locally R_Z⊗_A^L P with P a bounded finite-projective A-complex. Assume L is bounded above. We prove C_S(i_*L). Throughout, for a weakly etale site object W→S with Z_W=Z×_S W and i_W:Z_W→W, [lem-exc-closed-localization] (the cartesian square of W→S and i) gives (i_*F)|_W≅i_{W,*}(F|_{Z_W}) and identifies the two composite inverse images (i^{-1}F)|_{Z_W}≅i_W^{-1}(F|_W); applied to the ring sheaf R this identifies R_Z|_{Z_W} with i_W^{-1}(R|_W), so the hypothesis on L and the conclusion restrict to W with the same kind of coefficients. By step 3 we can first replace S by an affine open S'; the complement of Z∩S' in S' is V∩S', quasi-compact since V→S is quasi-compact (V is quasi-compact and S quasi-separated). Refine a trivializing cover of Z by a finite cover of affine ind-etale objects Z_a→Z, using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. The lift v of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties] gives affine pro-etale S_a=v(Z_a)→S with S_a×_S Z=Z_a. Together with V these S_a cover S: they cover every point of Z and V covers its complement. They are a finite family of qcqs objects. On V, i_*L is zero. On S_a it is i_{a,*}(R_{Z_a}⊗_A^L P_a), with i_a:Z_a→S_a and R_{Z_a}=R_Z|_{Z_a}. This base-change identity is the restriction isomorphism of [lem-exc-closed-localization] for W=S_a (on sections it is (i_*F)(W)=F(W×_S Z) of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]); both closed pushforwards are exact because the complements are quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], so it holds termwise on representing complexes. Put P_{S_a}=R_{S_a}⊗_A P_a, with R_{S_a}=R|_{S_a}, and h_a:S_a\Z_a→S_a. By the inverse-image identification above, R_{Z_a}≅i_a^{-1}R_{S_a}, and exact inverse image commutes with tensoring by each finite projective term (a retract of a finite free module), so i_a^{-1}P_{S_a}=P_{S_a}|_{Z_a}≅R_{Z_a}⊗_A P_a. The localization short exact sequences of the same open-closed node, applied termwise, give the triangle h_{a,!}(P_{S_a}|_{S_a\Z_a})→P_{S_a}→i_{a,*}(P_{S_a}|_{Z_a}). Steps 4 and 5 put its first two vertices in C_{S_a}, so its third is in C_{S_a}. Step 3 now proves C_S(i_*L). Notice that the trivializing cover was lifted from Z to ambient site objects; no assertion that internal Hom commutes with arbitrary closed inverse image is made.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14, final paragraph: lifting a trivializing cover of a closed stratum and the triangle h_!M→M→K

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to K. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite extension E, noetherian finite-dimensional T, invertibility of ℓ, and the completed A_T-module category in the statement. It gives boundedness of K and a finite stratification on which K is pro-etale locally A_T⊗_A^L P for perfect A-complexes P. Restrictions here use the same completed ring sheaf, not constant A coefficients or rational E coefficients. Refine this finite stratification to a finite filtration by closed subsets with locally perfect layers. Explicitly, express each stratum as an open intersected with a closed subset and list the finitely many opens involved (including complements of those closed subsets). The subset F_k of points belonging to at most k of these opens is closed: its complement is the union of the intersections of k+1 opens. On F_k\F_{k-1} the membership patterns form a finite clopen partition, each piece lying in one original stratum. Thus the restriction of K to every layer is locally perfect. If m is the number of listed opens, set F_{-1}=∅ and |F_m|=|T|; give every F_k for 0≤k≤m its reduced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Thus F_m is T_red, while its open complement is empty. Each membership-pattern piece of a layer maps to its original stratum: the piece is open in the reduced scheme F_k\F_{k-1}, hence reduced; the stratum's immersion is a closed immersion into an open W of T containing the stratum, the piece lies in W, and its image lies in that of the closed immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives the factorization of the piece through the stratum scheme over T. Exact inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] carries a local finite-projective tensor description to its pullback: each finite-projective term is a retract of a finite free module, so pulling back its splitting gives the same tensor description with the pulled-back ring. Thus the locally perfect assertion survives this scheme-theoretic refinement, using inverse-image coefficients throughout. Every complement used is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], since T is noetherian; the same applies to its intersections with affine opens, so the complementary open immersions are quasi-compact morphisms. In any qcqs pro-etale base change these complements remain quasi-compact, so all preceding steps remain applicable there.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 via Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); finite stratification refinement for the devissage in Lemma 6.3.14

proof.text: Put U_k=T\F_k for -1≤k≤m, so U_{-1}=T and U_m=∅. Let j_k:U_k→T be the open immersion and L_k=j_{k,!}(K|_{U_k}). For each 0≤k≤m, the layer Y_k=F_k\F_{k-1} is closed in U_{k-1}; write i_k:Y_k→U_{k-1} and h_k:U_k→U_{k-1}. Its open complement is quasi-compact. Apply the localization short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] termwise to K|_{U_{k-1}}, then apply the exact functor j_{k-1,!}. This gives a triangle L_k→L_{k-1}→j_{k-1,!}i_{k,*}(K|_{Y_k}). The identification of its first vertex uses the adjunctions of the same open-closed node: for module sheaves F on U_k and G on T, Hom(j_{k-1,!}h_{k,!}F,G)=Hom(h_{k,!}F,j_{k-1}^{-1}G)=Hom(F,h_k^{-1}j_{k-1}^{-1}G)=Hom(F,j_k^{-1}G). Thus j_{k-1,!}h_{k,!} and j_{k,!} are canonically isomorphic as left adjoints to j_k^{-1}. This natural identification respects the counits, and exactness permits applying it termwise to complexes. The inverse-image restrictions compose, with coefficients always the inverse image of A_T. By step 7, K|_{Y_k} is locally perfect and bounded above. Step 6 puts i_{k,*}(K|_{Y_k}) in C_{U_{k-1}}, and step 5 puts the third vertex in C_T. Start with L_m=0, which lies in C_T by the definition, and descend in k using step 4 and these triangles to obtain L_{-1}=K in C_T. This uses localization only on the complementary opens, and requires no closed inverse-image base-change identity.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14, reduction to a locally closed stratum and its open-closed factorization; applied as instructed by Lemma 6.8.12

proof.text: Take the qcqs site object W=T in C_T(K) from step 8. This gives precisely the canonical global derived Hom comparison in the statement, with the given common lower bound N. All previous calculations allowed every integer N, so the shift from D^{≥0} in the source has already been included. They identify maps induced by coprojections throughout; consequently the isomorphism is the specified canonical map. The complexes and maps are A-linear, so the isomorphism holds in D(A), not merely on underlying groups. The empty family gives 0→0. No completeness or constructibility was imposed on the target family M_i or on its coproduct.
